discovery: Optical metamaterials and metasurfaces: engineered nanostructured media that control light beyond the limits of natural materials
motivation: Pendry showed theoretically that sub-wavelength resonant structures can give effective permittivity and permeability unavailable in nature, predicting negative refraction, the perfect lens and transformation optics. Smith provided the decisive experimental demonstrations of negative-index media and the first electromagnetic cloak, establishing metamaterials as real physics rather than speculation. Capasso introduced the generalized laws of reflection and refraction with phase-gradient metasurfaces (2011), turning the concept into flat, ultrathin optics - metalenses, holograms and polarization optics - now entering industrial production in imaging and sensing. Together they created a new paradigm: light-matter interaction designed at the nanoscale by geometry, not chemistry. The field has transformed optics research worldwide, connecting fundamental electrodynamics to technologies in imaging, communications, energy harvesting and optical computing. It exemplifies the rare combination of conceptual originality, experimental elegance and broad technological reach the Nobel Prize recognizes.
